claim:s1-metabolic-partnership.proposition: An archaeal-bacterial association can become mutually beneficial under restricted redox and substrate regimes — partner-dependent growth emerges on feasible, mass-balanced metabolite exchange — but the benefit is not necessarily stable or obligate, and it disappears outside the feasible regime and under alternative gap-fills.
claim:s1-metabolic-partnership.hypothesis: Under at least one field-consistent redox/substrate regime, a reconstructed archaeal-host / bacterial-partner pair achieves partner-dependent growth (each grows better together than alone) on mass-balanced exchange fluxes, while a no-exchange / parasitic control does not.

provenance.note: Ratio of community biomass flux to the best single-member flux; >1.1 = a >10% mutualistic advantage. Threshold is a pre-registered hypothesis to be calibrated against Imachi-2020 syntrophic growth once the GEMs are built.
Exchange fluxes must conserve C/N/O/H and charge by construction.

claim:s2-ecology-to-proximity.proposition: Selection may favor sustained contact: in spatially structured (finite-diffusion) environments the S1 cross-feeding advantage is distance-dependent and favors persistent proximity, creating a precondition for intimate symbiosis — but the advantage vanishes under high diffusion / well-mixed conditions, so proximity selection is contingent on spatial structure.
claim:s2-ecology-to-proximity.hypothesis: Below a critical diffusion length the cross-feeding fitness advantage is distance-dependent and selects for sustained contact; under well-mixed (high-diffusion) conditions the proximity advantage collapses, so selection for contact is a spatial-structure effect, not a given.

provenance.note: Slope of fitness vs -separation (normalized); >0.1 = a measurable distance-dependent advantage. Calibrate against S2 parameter priors from Radler-2026 protrusion length scales.

claim:s3-protrusions-to-enclosure.proposition: Physical enclosure is a separate hurdle from metabolic benefit: observed protrusion mechanics can, under restricted geometry and bending-cost regimes, reach stable wrapping — but a beneficial symbiosis (S1/S2) need not imply ingestive ability, and some topologies never enclose within realistic area/energy budgets.
claim:s3-protrusions-to-enclosure.hypothesis: Under cryo-ET-constrained bending moduli and observed protrusion timescales, at least one topology (classical engulfment or inside-out wrapping) reaches a stable enclosed state with conserved membrane area and a finite energy budget, while a no-enclosure control does not.

provenance.note: Fraction of parameterized runs reaching stable enclosure; >0.5 within the cryo-ET-constrained regime. Priors from Rodrigues-Oliveira-2023 and Radler-2026.

claim:s4-compartmental-energetic-couplin.proposition: An enclosed partner may develop organelle-like function only under restricted physiological conditions: internalization yields a net ATP/biomass benefit solely where export exceeds transport, upkeep, and conflict costs, bounded by proton-gradient constraints — and there exist regimes where internalization is energetically harmful relative to external association.
claim:s4-compartmental-energetic-couplin.hypothesis: Internalization is net energy-positive only in a restricted regime: where symbiont ATP export exceeds the host's transport + upkeep + conflict costs. Outside that regime, an externally associated partner (S2) has equal or higher net fitness.

provenance.note: Net ATP flux (internalized) minus net ATP flux (external association), per biomass; >0 in at least one regime. Enzyme/pathway ancestry priors from Santana-Molina-2025.

claim:s5-symbiont-to-organelle.proposition: Integration becomes heritable and coordinated — a new evolutionary individual emerges — only when vertical-transmission fidelity and host-symbiont fitness alignment both cross threshold, after which gene loss is irreversible and the partner becomes obligate; configurations with survival but low transmission fidelity do NOT cross into heritable individuality.
claim:s5-symbiont-to-organelle.hypothesis: Stable heritable integration requires high-fidelity vertical transmission AND host-symbiont fitness alignment together; gene loss becomes irreversible (partner-removal lethal) only after transmission fidelity crosses a threshold. Within-host survival alone does not produce a new evolutionary unit.

provenance.note: Fraction of daughter hosts retaining a viable symbiont over >=50 generations; >0.95 = stable vertical inheritance. Threshold pre-registered; refine against population-genetics theory.

narrative.question: Under what physical, metabolic, ecological, and evolutionary conditions can a symbiotic association between an archaeal host and a bacterial partner transition into an integrated eukaryotic cell? The aim is not to animate a predetermined history but to identify plausible, impossible, and still-unresolved pathways from ecological association to a new evolutionary individual.

units.proposition: An archaeal-bacterial association can become mutually beneficial under restricted redox and substrate regimes — partner-dependent growth emerges on feasible, mass-balanced metabolite exchange — but the benefit is not necessarily stable or obligate, and it disappears outside the feasible regime and under alternative gap-fills.

Selection may favor sustained contact: in spatially structured (finite-diffusion) environments the S1 cross-feeding advantage is distance-dependent and favors persistent proximity, creating a precondition for intimate symbiosis — but the advantage vanishes under high diffusion / well-mixed conditions, so proximity selection is contingent on spatial structure.

Physical enclosure is a separate hurdle from metabolic benefit: observed protrusion mechanics can, under restricted geometry and bending-cost regimes, reach stable wrapping — but a beneficial symbiosis (S1/S2) need not imply ingestive ability, and some topologies never enclose within realistic area/energy budgets.

An enclosed partner may develop organelle-like function only under restricted physiological conditions: internalization yields a net ATP/biomass benefit solely where export exceeds transport, upkeep, and conflict costs, bounded by proton-gradient constraints — and there exist regimes where internalization is energetically harmful relative to external association.

Integration becomes heritable and coordinated — a new evolutionary individual emerges — only when vertical-transmission fidelity and host-symbiont fitness alignment both cross threshold, after which gene loss is irreversible and the partner becomes obligate; configurations with survival but low transmission fidelity do NOT cross into heritable individuality.

decisions.title: Which two or more candidate archaeal-host / bacterial-partner genome pairs anchor S1 (e.g. Asgard + alphaproteobacterium selections from GTDB/NCBI), and under which redox / substrate regimes (anaerobic, micro-aerobic) are they first tested?
decisions.detail: No single extant isolate is the ancestral host; S1 must reconstruct two or more pairs with explicit uncertainty rather than pick one.

decisions.title: Which initial ecology (syntrophy, commensalism, parasitism) is the primary scenario for S2, and which are the competing scenarios run head to head?
decisions.detail: Section 7 requires testing alternative initial ecologies, not assuming syntrophy.
